column4: Skip apples with rough, scab-like patches at the stem end.
column6: Apple is on the Non-GMO High-Risk List, and a peel study found residue fell when the peel came off. Organic bars GMOs.

column4: Press the narrow neck by the stem, which should give slightly.
column6: Pears are eaten with the skin on, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Grapes should hang firmly on green stems, not brown ones.
column6: MedlinePlus names grapes as thin-skinned fruit worth buying organic, and the whole berry is eaten.

column4: Look for fuzzy peach skin in red or yellow.
column6: MedlinePlus names peaches and nectarines as thin-skinned fruit worth buying organic.

column4: A white or gray sheen on the skin is natural, so leave it.
column6: The plum is eaten skin and all, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Pick shiny, dark cherries with green stems still attached.
column6: Cherries are eaten whole, skin included, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Skip berries with white or green shoulders around the caps.
column6: MedlinePlus names strawberries as thin-skinned fruit worth buying organic, and the whole berry is eaten.

column4: Look for a silver-white frost on the skin and no leaves in the box.
column6: Blueberries are eaten whole, skin included, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Read the label for the word wild or lowbush.
column6: The seal still applies to wild-labelled berries; frozen wild is the usual way to buy them.

column4: Check the clamshell bottom for juice stains.
column6: Raspberries and blackberries are eaten whole with no peel, and organic rules bar synthetic substances in growing.

column4: Pick firm, thick-walled, brightly colored peppers with a fresh green stem.
column6: The pepper wall and skin are eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Skip tomatoes with blotchy green or brown patches on the skin.
column6: The skin is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Read the bin sign for the word waxed before deciding to peel.
column5: Peel only if the cucumber is waxed.
column6: Cucumber skin is often eaten, and waxed cucumbers must be signed at the bin; organic rules bar synthetic inputs in growing.

column4: Run a finger along the pod and skip lumpy sections.
column6: The whole pod is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Choose snap pods that look plump and snug around the peas.
column6: The whole pod is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Pick pods about 2 to 4 inches long, not dull or shriveled.
column6: The whole pod is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Pick eggplant that feels relatively light for its size, with shiny skin.
column6: Eggplant is on the Non-GMO High-Risk List, and the skin is eaten. Organic bars GMOs.

column4: Skip any potato with a green tint on the skin.
column5: Throw away any sprouts and never eat potato that is green below the skin.
column6: Potato is on the Non-GMO High-Risk List, and the skin is often eaten. Organic bars GMOs.

column4: Pick small to medium sweet potatoes with even, deep-colored skin and no holes.
column6: Sweet potatoes grow in the soil, which organic rules require be managed with rotations and cover crops.

column4: Skip carrots with large green areas at the top.
column6: Carrots grow in the soil, which organic rules require be managed with rotations and cover crops.

column4: Pick small beets with a slender tap root and leaf stems still attached.
column6: Beets grow in the soil, which organic rules require be managed with rotations and cover crops.

column4: Pick brightly colored radishes still topped with fresh green leaves.
column6: Radishes grow in the soil and are eaten skin and all; organic rules require rotations and cover crops.

column4: Skip turnips with many leaf scars ringing the top.
column6: Turnips grow in the soil, which organic rules require be managed with rotations and cover crops.

column4: Split a stalk apart and look for pale to bright green, crisp inside.
column6: Celery stalks are eaten whole, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Skip kohlrabi bulbs with cracks or brown spots; attached leaves should be firm.
column6: Kohlrabi grows in the soil, which organic rules require be managed with rotations and cover crops.

column4: Choose a piece with few knobs and little branching.
column6: Ginger grows in the soil, which organic rules require be managed with rotations and cover crops.

column4: Snap off a small knob and it should break apart easily.
column6: Turmeric is a soil-grown root, and organic rules require rotations and cover crops in soil management.

column4: Pick spinach with broad, crisp, dark green leaves.
column6: The whole leaf is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Choose dark kale with small to medium leaves.
column6: The whole leaf is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Skip extremely solid, pale heads, which are mostly core.
column6: The whole leaf is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Press the top of the head and avoid hard bumps.
column6: The head is eaten leaf by leaf, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Look for red, pink, orange, yellow or white stems.
column6: The leaf and stem are both eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Look for bright green cilantro or deep-green parsley leaves.
column6: Herb leaves are eaten raw and unpeeled, and organic rules bar synthetic substances in growing.

column4: Look for smooth, whole, brightly colored basil leaves.
column6: Basil leaves are eaten raw and unpeeled, and organic rules bar synthetic substances in growing.

column4: Check that leaves and stems both look crisp, not limp.
column6: Microgreens are eaten whole, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Reject any tub holding dry or slimy sprouts.
column6: Sprouts are eaten whole and raw, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Skip heads whose flower ends part easily or show yellow blooms.
column6: The florets are eaten whole, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Skip heads with gaps between the curds.
column6: The curds are eaten whole, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Look for bright green heads with white stem ends.
column6: The whole sprout is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Skip heads that are oblong or cracked.
column6: The leaves are eaten whole, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Choose spears with tips firmly closed.
column6: The whole spear is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Peek under the cap for pink or light tan gills.
column6: The whole cap is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Choose leeks with fresh green tops and necks no thicker than 1.5 inches.
column6: Leeks are eaten from white base to green top, and organic rules bar synthetic substances in growing.

column4: Stem colour varies, so light green stalks can still be good.
column5: Cut off and discard the leaves.
column6: The stalk is eaten, and organic rules bar synthetic substances and GMOs in growing.

column4: Check the silk ends for decay or worm damage.
column6: Corn is on the Non-GMO High-Risk List, with 94% of US corn genetically modified. Organic bars GMOs.

column4: Pick squash about 4 inches long with bright, healthy skin.
column6: Zucchini and yellow squash are on the Non-GMO High-Risk List, and the skin is eaten. Organic bars GMOs.

column4: Look for some yellow streaks on the skin.
column6: Papaya is on the Non-GMO High-Risk List, with modified fruit in the produce section. Organic bars GMOs.

column4: Check for slight green at the stem and tip.
column6: The peel is discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Skip avocados with large indentations in the skin.
column6: The skin is discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Look for a smooth, rounded scar where the stem was.
column6: The rind is discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Choose pale yellow to light lemon skin with little green.
column6: The rind is discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Turn it over and look for a yellow, not white, underside.
column6: The rind is discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Check that the crown leaves look fresh, not dry and brown.
column6: Pineapple is on the Non-GMO High-Risk List, with a modified pink variety on sale. Organic bars GMOs.

column4: Skip mangoes with sap on the skin.
column6: The skin is discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Press lightly: ripe kiwi releases to gentle pressure.
column6: The skin is discarded or eaten, and organic is the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Pick oranges and grapefruit heavy for their size, with smooth skin.
column6: The peel is discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: For limes, look for smooth, glossy dark green skin.
column5: If the zest is used, buy organic.
column6: The zest is eaten, so organic matters for the peel: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Look for a slightly square shape, not perfectly round.
column6: The rind is discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Check the neck: small and dry, with no moisture.
column6: The dry skins are discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Choose heavy bulbs that stay closed, with dry outer skins.
column6: The papery skins are discarded, but organic is still the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.

column4: Check the stem: it should be dry and firm.
column6: The shell is discarded or eaten, and organic is the default: organic rules (7 CFR 205.105) bar synthetic substances, GMOs, irradiation and sewage sludge in growing.
